# FDG8031

> DO use byte arrays instead of collections of bytes.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.3 Choosing Between Arrays and Collections.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8031
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Use a byte array instead of '{0}' in the signature of '{1}'

Test profile: test classes are public only for the test framework; their signatures are not API. FDG8031 reports a collection of bytes, a type that implements ICollection<byte> or IReadOnlyCollection<byte> (such as Collection<byte>, List<byte> or IList<byte>) other than byte[] and ArraySegment<byte> or ImmutableArray<byte>, which are views over a byte array with its memory footprint and element access, the reasons section 8.3.3 gives for arrays, as the type of a parameter, a return value or the result of a returned Task<T> or ValueTask<T>, a property or indexer, or a field of an externally visible member. IEnumerable<byte> is not reported: FDG8018 prefers it for parameters, and it is not a stored collection. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Span<byte> and Memory<byte>, the more performant designs of the body, are not collections. Coverage is partial. Changing the type changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
// bad design
public Collection<byte> ReadBytes() { ... }

// good design
public byte[] ReadBytes() { ... }

// more performant good designs (see 9.12)
public int ReadBytes(byte[] destination) { ... }
public int ReadBytes(Span<byte> destination) { ... }
```
